WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW   What you already know
Many MENA companies publish sustainability or ESG reports, and some now apply IFRS S1 and S2. An integrated report is different: it connects financial and non-financial information in one concise story of value creation. Section 18.6 explains the relationship.

EXAM TRAP   Audience trap
The primary audience is providers of financial capital, not 'all stakeholders'. All stakeholders benefit, but the Framework names investors and lenders first.

WORKED EXAMPLE   Worked example: the irrigation trade-off
Step 1. Suppose Orontes spends $2,000,000 on drip irrigation for its groves: financial capital falls and manufactured capital rises.
Step 2. Water use falls by 150,000 m³, about 17% of the total: natural capital is preserved.
Step 3. Orontes trains 400 cooperative farmers to use the system: human and social and relationship capital rise.
Check. An integrated report explains the whole trade-off, not only the cost.

FALSE-FRIEND ALERT   Capitals, رؤوس الأموال, capitaux
In integrated reporting, capitals are resources and relationships, not share capital. French capital social means share capital, but capital social et relationnel is one of the six capitals. Read the whole phrase.

EXAM TRAP   Seven or eight?
There are seven guiding principles (how to report) and eight content elements (what to report). Materiality and connectivity are principles; governance, business model and outlook are content elements.

WATCH: NOT YET TESTABLE   Not tested: climate rules
The SEC's 2024 climate disclosure rule never took effect; it is stayed, and the SEC proposed to rescind it in 2026. Some MENA markets now require ISSB-based disclosures, for example Qatar from 2026 and the largest Amman Stock Exchange companies from 2026. These are background facts, not exam content.
